issues.title: F01 - bind a sealed weight package to a publisher-signed manifest digest
issues.body:
**Claim.** An approved model label must not be attachable to different sealed weights.

**Read first.** `govsim/sealing.py:60-81`, `govsim/governor.py:549-566` and `:586-604`, `govsim/gpu.py:145-155`, `govsim/cluster.py:303-304`, `govsim/origin_gate.py:99-109`.

**Concrete failure.** With model M already in `sealed_models`, keep a genuine publisher manifest and evaluator statement for M. Choose different weight bytes W', make a new DEK, encrypt W', label the package M and set its `plain_sha256` to hash(W'). Seal the new DEK to the governor's public KEK (anyone with the public key can). BEGIN_MODEL approves the authentic M manifest; KEY_RELEASE approves M and unwraps the supplied DEK; the GPU checks W' against the hash supplied in that same substituted package and runs W' as M. AES-GCM proves integrity of the chosen package under the chosen key; it does not prove those bytes were approved.

**Fix.** Define one canonical publisher-signed manifest that commits to the exact weight bytes (commitment, total length, chunk ordering, format, execution-relevant config). Bind the evaluator statement, policy entry, DEK envelope and lease to that manifest digest. The protected GPU loader must verify the decrypted content against the authenticated commitment before enabling execution. A manifest that commits only to a name or version is insufficient.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f01_weight_manifest_binding.py`). With one valid signed/evaluated manifest, replace ciphertext, DEK and plaintext hash together while preserving the approved label; execution must stay disabled. A genuine package must succeed. A package for another valid manifest, relabelled, must fail. Cover truncation, chunk duplication and config substitution as separate mutations of the same authenticated object.

issues.title: F02 - one current-policy validity predicate for release, renewal and commit
issues.body:
**Claim.** A revoked GPU must not obtain a fresh key release, and a replayed lease must not revive execution.

**Read first.** `govsim/governor.py:269-273`, `:538-540`, `:578-633`; `govsim/gpu.py:122-173`; `govsim/origin_gate.py:63-76` and `:126-147`.

**Concrete failure.** Attest GPU A, begin M, get a 30s lease. Commit a valid new policy that keeps M but revokes A. The governor zeroizes the key but keeps A's cached attestation. A fresh host-signed KEY_RELEASE under the new epoch is accepted: `_attested()` checks only cache existence and expiry, and KEY_RELEASE checks the model allowlist but not current GPU revocations, so it issues a new lease. Releasing repeatedly can extend operation through the one-hour attestation cache. Separately, replaying an old authentic key box and lease before its original expiry restores execution, because `install_key()` has no epoch/revocation floor.

**Fix.** One current-policy validity predicate for every attestation-dependent operation: check current chip and signing-key revocations, reference validity and model authorization on release, renewal and relevant commits; invalidate affected caches on policy change. At the GPU, keep a protected authorization generation or revocation floor, advance it before zeroization, and reject older leases and key boxes. Bind each box to its lease/session and enforce expiry through a trusted timer, including while idle.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f02_revoke_release.py`). Revoke A while M stays allowed: a fresh release with a new sequence, current epoch, authentic envelope and still-live cache must be denied with no key material; a replayed old box/lease after revocation must be denied; a non-revoked control still works; an idle lease expires without calling run_tokens().

issues.title: F04 - enforce the beneficiary registry on the small-payment path
issues.body:
**Claim.** A new beneficiary must not receive automatic payment authority; the rulebook's declared 'new beneficiary is a hold' must actually hold.

**Read first.** `govsim/cluster.py:140-175` and `:218-225`, `govsim/policy.py:218-260`, `govsim/endpoints.py:129` and `:142-186`, `govsim/road_reachability.py:32-59`, `results/road-reachability.md:15-37`.

issues.title: F05 - payer consent and operator approval are separate conjunctive predicates
issues.body:
**Claim.** Turning on human approval must not silently turn off the payer's own confirmation.

**Read first.** `govsim/cluster.py:135-144`, `govsim/governor.py:698-723` and `:892-922`, `govsim/customer_confirm.py:26-85`, `results/customer-confirm.md:23-25`.

**Concrete failure.** Enable both `payer_confirm_payments=True` and `sandbox=True`. The small-payment rule keeps its payer-confirmation requirement but becomes a human-mode rule, and the request handler explicitly skips `_payer_confirmed()` in human mode (`... and req_mode != "human"`). A hold is created without the payer's signature; the operator quorum approves; `_cmd_approve()` mints the ticket without checking payer consent.

**Fix.** Represent payer consent and operator approval as separate conjunctive predicates. Retain the consent commitment and expiry with the hold and revalidate it against the current registry before release/commit. If an emergency role may override payer consent, make that a separate, logged permission. Reject unsupported combinations at policy load.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f05_payer_consent.py`). All four combinations of sandbox and payer-confirm. With both on, operator quorum alone must not mint a ticket; adding the payer's current request-bound confirmation permits it; an expired confirmation during the hold forces the specified reauthorization.

issues.title: F06 - validate registries and policy expiry against trusted time on every use
issues.body:
**Claim.** Installed authority must not outlive its freshness rules.

**Read first.** `govsim/governor.py:282-291`, `:821-836`, `:1306-1336`, `:244-245`; `govsim/policy.py:248-258`; `docs/25-the-rulebook-and-the-board.md:229-231`; `tests/test_h07_register.py:25-30`.

**Concrete failure.** Install a genuinely signed recipient registry for A expiring at t+1. Installation computes `stale=False`. At t+2 a message to A still takes the auto path, because the rule consults the cached boolean, not the clock. The customer registry has the same defect. `install_list()` has no per-list version/high-water check, so an older still-unexpired list can replace a newer one. An installed policy can run past its own expiry while other liveness holds.

**Fix.** Store authenticated list identity, version, expiry and issuer; compare expiry with trusted time on every relevant use; keep durable per-list version floors; filter revoked signers. Bind held decisions to their authority versions. Enforce policy expiry as a specified fail-closed transition, not an undocumented continued-running exception.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f06_registry_aging.py`). Success before a 1s list expiry, hold/denial afterward without reinstalling; same for payer registries and held approvals; replacing a newer list with an older signed list is refused; a revoked signer is rejected; heartbeats alive across policy expiry force the declared safe transition before another effect.

issues.title: F10 - response commitments are immutable and scoped to one identity
issues.body:
**Claim.** One unsampled response ID must not suppress all later random audit draws.

**Read first.** `govsim/governor.py:1032-1044`, `:674-676`, `:732-738`, `:769-773`; `govsim/cluster.py:420-424` and `:450-455`; `tests/test_h18_oversight.py:22-65`.

**Concrete failure.** Find a response ID that released without an escrow receipt. Submit different response bytes under that same ID: `_record_stream()` overwrites hashes but keeps the earlier `sampled=False` (it uses `setdefault()` and only draws when unset), so no receipt is required and there is never another draw for that identifier.

**Fix.** Make each response commitment immutable and scoped to workload instance, epoch, authenticated session and response ID. A different hash under an existing identity is rejected. Record terminal release state. A retry keeps its commitment's draw; new content gets a new commitment and a new draw.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f10_response_commitment.py`). With a deterministic RNG that returns unsampled once then sampled: release the first response, replace its bytes under the same ID, require rejection or a fresh sample tied to a new identity; a legitimate retry cannot change the committed hash or erase a sampled result.

issues.title: F11 - atomic admit-and-consume at the endpoint
issues.body:
**Claim.** At-most-once endpoint execution must not depend on an unstated single-thread assumption.

**Read first.** `govsim/endpoints.py:160-186`, `govsim/governor.py:932-956`, `hardware_ref` has the locked pattern at `endpoints.py:96-117` (reference).

**Concrete failure.** For one valid unbudgeted messaging ticket, callers A and B both complete `admit()` before either writes the consumed set; both persist the same consumed entry and both append an effect, because this ticket has no reservation to consume and no central single-use record.

**Fix.** Specify the endpoint concurrency contract and make admission plus durable consumption atomic through a lock, a transactional compare-and-set, or an equivalent. Preserve atomic ownership through the effect-dispatch decision. For an external provider, map the ticket to a provider-enforced idempotency key and define crash reconciliation; a local consumed flag cannot make an arbitrary remote side effect transactional.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f11_atomic_consume.py`). Force two calls to pause right after successful admission, release both; exactly one crosses the effect boundary. Use a ticket with no budget reservation. Test recovery after consumption but before the outcome is known.

issues.title: F07 - the attestation token must bind an ephemeral request-signing key
issues.body:
**Claim.** An attested workload's later requests must not be forgeable by anyone holding a copy of its token (it must not be a bearer credential).

**Read first.** `hardware_ref/attest.py:272-292`, `hardware_ref/gate.py:167-180`, `hardware_ref/system.py:174-181` and `:89-95`, `hardware_ref/attacks.py:697-703`.

**Concrete failure.** Copy an authentic token and its public measurement string; from another process submit a permitted automatic http.post with a fresh request ID. The gate verifies the token signature, expiry and measurement-string equality (supplied by the caller) but requires no signature from a key bound to the attested workload.

**Fix.** Include an attested ephemeral request-signing key (or authenticated channel binding) in the token, with a gate audience and session identity. Require a signature over the canonical action, parameters, sequence, audience and policy context. Define how revocation and reference changes invalidate the session. Reuse SG's host-signed-command pattern rather than keeping two origin guarantees.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f07_token_binding.py`). An adversarial process with only the public token and measurement fails; a request signed by the attested session key succeeds; cross-gate, cross-session and replay all fail.

issues.title: F08 - persist the revocation high-water mark across verifier restart
issues.body:
**Claim.** A reconstructed verifier must not accept hardware that was revoked before it restarted.

**Read first.** `hardware_ref/attest.py:35-46`, `:98-140`, `:61-74`, `:223-224`, `:242-293`; `tests/test_audit_2026_10_22.py:142-161`; `hardware_ref/system.py:139-166`.

**Concrete failure.** Verifier V installs L2 revoking device D, then is destroyed. V2 is built with the same pinned roots and reloads the older authentic R1/L1; `_high_water` initializes empty, so V2 accepts the old documents and then accepts D on a fresh challenge.

**Fix.** Persist each active configuration with its authenticated version/digest high-water mark and restore atomically before any appraisal. A new install needs an authenticated minimum version, a retained checkpoint, or a bootstrap protocol. Block issuance if recovery cannot establish freshness.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f08_cold_verifier.py`). Revoke an instantiated device, persist, destroy and reconstruct the verifier, supply the old authentic documents: appraisal stays blocked or rejects D; current documents and an unrevoked device succeed; include same-version conflicting documents and a power interruption between the two persistence steps.

issues.title: F22 - the audit verifier needs a pinned key and a retained checkpoint
issues.body:
**Claim.** An authenticated audit verdict must not be forgeable with the export's own trust anchor, nor satisfiable by a stripped authentic prefix.

**Read first.** `hardware_ref/audit.py:211-212` and `:225-269`, `hardware_ref/cli.py:152-175`, `hardware_ref/attacks.py:557-595`, `tests/test_audit.py:32-65`, `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:84-91`.

**Concrete failure.** (1) Replace the whole export with records signed by an attacker key and put that key in `doc["pub"]`; `verify_export()` trusts the key from the same file it verifies, so it prints OK. (2) Keep the real key and a genuine prefix, delete the tail and all checkpoints; the chain verifier accepts the prefix and the checkpoint loop runs zero times, so it prints OK.

**Fix.** Authenticated verification takes an independently pinned gate key and log identity plus a retained authenticated minimum checkpoint, and verifies consistency with it. Keep a self-consistency mode but label its result explicitly as internal consistency, not authenticated history. A pinned key alone still permits prefix rollback.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f22_audit_verifier.py`). Under a real pinned key and retained checkpoint, reject the attacker-key replacement, the stripped-prefix export and an older authentic export; accept the current history and a valid append-only extension; test self-consistency mode separately.

issues.title: F12 - account every permitted channel against the containment ceiling
issues.body:
**Claim.** A finite-byte containment ceiling must account for every externally observable channel, including message bodies and other permitted parameters.

**Read first.** `govsim/containment.py:43-64`, `govsim/cluster.py:162-164` and `:219-225`, `govsim/governor.py:704-725`, `audit/wave-2/P3.revise-2.comment.md:9-18`, `results/containment.md:35-40`.

**Concrete failure.** While RUN, consume the output allowance, then send `message.send` to a listed recipient with an arbitrary string in an unconstrained body. The auto rule bounds the recipient but not length/bytes/rate, and the endpoint adds no check, so the model has no finite byte ceiling on this channel. EXPERIMENT-CONTAINMENT measures neither this path nor information in other parameters, adds a one-time unpresented allowance to a per-hour rate, and describes a rack ceiling from a single governor.

**Fix.** Maintain a complete inventory of observable channels (typed actions and downstream relays); define schemas, payload bounds and destination semantics; count all applicable bytes against a shared accounting scope; an unbounded channel must make the finite-ceiling assertion fail. Report burst allowance and sustained rate separately.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f12_containment_channels.py`). Consume the output allowance, then deliver messaging tickets while counting bytes at the receiving endpoint; across all governors and approved forwarders the finite-ceiling assertion must fail until the body channel is bounded, and hold once it is.

issues.title: F13 - P3b must install the policies it names and measure delivered bytes
issues.body:
**Claim.** The containment experiment must measure the policies it claims and bytes actually released, not signing calls under the default policy.

**Read first.** `govsim/containment.py:32-64` and `:91-110`, `govsim/cluster.py:89-104`, `:268-277`, `:420-468`, `results/containment.md:11-33`, `tests/test_p3b_containment.py:6-15`.

The recorded 6,135 and 26,200 bytes are exactly the loop and default-policy values. `sign_output()` records a provenance signature; it does not release bytes through egress.

**Fix.** Supply policy parameters at construction, or sign/commit/reload after changing them, and assert the installed policy identity and each limit. Retract the 50-year/centuries/11-day interpretations pending corrected measurement.

Three deliberately distinct policies, with the live policy identity and limits asserted; the 4,096-byte case never exceeds its signed allowance; an actual sandbox peer request is attempted; a signature with no egress release contributes zero delivered bytes.

issues.title: F23 - price the per-response-release signature on the complete path
issues.body:
**Claim.** The engine-budget figure must include the signature on every response-release ticket, not only the batched record signatures.

**Read first.** `govsim/bench.py:21-36` and `:48-72`, `govsim/governor.py:880-889` and `:992-994`, `govsim/cluster.py:445-468`, `docs/04-specification.md:296-299`, `blog/08-the-chip-that-says-no-7-scaling-no.md:23` (HS), `tests/test_h09_overhead.py:1-20`.

**Concrete failure.** The benchmark calls `sign_output()` and prices batched record signatures, but never follows the response-release path, which requests a ticket for every response and signs every ticket (counted as `ops["ticket"]`, not `ops["sign"]`). Including those tickets, the modelled load is well over one engine at 100 tokens/response, versus the advertised ~34 percent.

**Fix.** Instrument every cryptographic operation on the full request-to-effect path and price the actual engine. If capacity fails, specify faster hardware, independently verifiable batch authorization with atomic per-item consumption, or a keyed endpoint MAC. Include hashing, verification, durable state, queues and overload behavior; a signature that arrives after release cannot authorize it.

**Discriminating test** (`tests/test_f23_response_signature_cost.py`). Run the full response API at 100 and 500 tokens/response across all slots; independently count tickets, signatures, verifications and releases and reconcile with the model; the reported utilization must include the release-ticket signatures.

issues.title: F04-audit - A1 must not call an enum a destination boundary
issues.body:
**Claim.** The reachability audit must not classify a rule as confined because a currency enum contains `in`, and its fixpoint must model external effects.

**Read first.** `govsim/road_reachability.py:47-59`, `:75-79`, `:117-127`, `results/road-reachability.md:15-37`.

**Concrete failure.** `classify()` calls a rule confined if any field has `in`/`in_list`/`not_in_list`; a `currency in [USD]` enum qualifies, so the unbounded-beneficiary payment rule is labelled confined. The supposed fixpoint calls `attempt()`, which only requests a ticket, then repeats without executing effects or modelling new accounts/routes.

**Fix.** Confinement requires a destination allowlist of the parties that may receive the effect, not any enum and not the complement of a denylist. issues.body:
